headland_lookout.label: Travancore headland and palm lookout
headland_lookout.anchor: The sandy Travancore headland, one tall palm with a rough rope-lashed lookout platform, and a path among coconut palms. If the boy is shown, he stays high on the platform. Sea-only views are from the shore observer's position, with all observers behind the camera; the establishing landscape contains no invented foreground figures. Where visible at the specified distance, the large ships are three-masted, square-rigged 18th-century Dutch East Indiamen with high sterns and painted gunport strakes, their flags plain red, white and blue horizontal bands without a monogram; do not enlarge distant detail. When Ibrahim is mounted, he rides a plain dark brown horse.
headland_lookout.absent: No foreign fort, tower or European buildings; no invented shore figures in an empty horizon view.
headland_lookout.time: hard midday sun and sea glare

flagship_at_sea.label: Dutch flagship offshore
flagship_at_sea.anchor: The largest Dutch East Indiaman offshore, high stern, quarterdeck and gunport strake, at the distance specified. Shore-to-ship spyglass views retain their soft circular vignette; the seaward reverse view is not a spyglass view. Only when the officer is specified, show a tiny dark-blue-coated figure with a black tricorne and pale hair at the collar, never a portrait. Where visible at the specified distance, the large ships are three-masted, square-rigged 18th-century Dutch East Indiamen with high sterns and painted gunport strakes, their flags plain red, white and blue horizontal bands without a monogram; do not enlarge distant detail.
flagship_at_sea.absent: No shore observer or lookout boy aboard, no close face, no extra named officer or legible flag emblem.

war_hall.label: Travancore map room and war hall
war_hall.anchor: The Travancore war hall under a tiled roof on timber pillars, laterite walls and a stone floor. Maps lie on the floor, weighted by stones and spear shafts, with pebbles and a white shell as tokens. Anyone seated or kneeling is directly on the floor at the map's edge; there is no raised map surface. Varma's spear lies aside. Nagoji remains kneeling in close-ups of his map-room conversation; the doorway arrival keeps him standing as described.
war_hall.absent: No chairs, benches, stools, raised map table, throne or foreign architecture. A specified memory alone may enter the scene. No turban or peacock crest on Varma here, whatever his reference sheet shows; only the narrow white cloth band over his pulled-back hair.

tengapattanam_pavilion.label: Tengapattanam beach pavilion, remembered audience
tengapattanam_pavilion.anchor: The open beach pavilion at Tengapattanam, timber posts and a simple sloping roof beside the sand. The king's seat is low and backless, local timber rather than a high-backed chair, and the governor sits across the low table on a matching low seat. For seated meeting views the low table holds open-wick lamps, interpreters kneel, and the visible guards stand behind the king's seat. The arrival view shows only the approaching procession and its reception, with no simultaneous seated audience. Any Deccan riders standing with Nagoji and Dhanaji wear plain off-white turbans and white sashes; only Nagoji wears the rust-red turban and red sash.
tengapattanam_pavilion.absent: No European throne or high-backed chair for anyone, no glass lamp chimneys or foreign stone palace. Do not add the seated meeting to the approach view.
tengapattanam_pavilion.time: night, half past eleven, torchlight and clay or brass oil lamps; a warmer, slightly faded flashback palette

audience_hall.label: Travancore coastal audience hall
audience_hall.anchor: A long Travancore coastal hall with timber pillars, tiled roof, woven floor mats, a low platform at the front and a cloth at the open seaward side. Seated attendees use floor mats. In the audience, the visitors' cleared mat space is on the king's own left of the platform, Ramayyan's place is on the king's own right, and the women's clusters extend from the front to the rear. Nagoji's side pillar is distinct from the rear pillar. He remains standing there in audience close-ups. In the dusk conversation both speakers sit on the same floor mat. Whole-room views without a named cast keep attendees distant and unidentifiable; do not add named people outside the specified crop. The interpreter is the same man in every view: mixed Portuguese and Indian features, bareheaded, a plain white cotton jacket over a dark lower cloth, empty-handed, never in an envoy's coat.
audience_hall.absent: No throne, chairs, benches, European interior, glass lamps or newly invented named attendees. The rear pillar where Ibrahim appears is separate from Nagoji's side pillar.
audience_hall.time: shaded daylight, open clay and brass oil lamps

courtyard_room.label: Small limewashed room off a Travancore courtyard
courtyard_room.anchor: A small limewashed room in the Travancore compound, open to a narrow courtyard, with tiled eaves, a stone floor, one plain low wooden stool and a clay water cup. The palm-leaf drawing lies on the floor; the stool never becomes a writing desk. Follow only the panel's present seated, rising or kneeling pose.
courtyard_room.absent: No European chair, table for the floor drawing, prison bars, uniform or coat on Karl.
courtyard_room.time: low slanting evening light from the narrow courtyard

coastal_ridge.label: Travancore ridge above the beach
coastal_ridge.anchor: The ridge above a Travancore beach, with a path for the two mounted observers and open views of the shallows, inland cart track and the offshore squadron. Nagoji and Ibrahim remain mounted during their spyglass exchange. A landscape-only view looks downhill from their position without showing them. Where visible at the specified distance, the large ships are three-masted, square-rigged 18th-century Dutch East Indiamen with high sterns and painted gunport strakes, their flags plain red, white and blue horizontal bands without a monogram; do not enlarge distant detail. When Ibrahim is mounted, he rides a plain dark brown horse.
coastal_ridge.absent: No invented foreground observers, fort, foreign buildings or ship deck on the ridge.
coastal_ridge.time: copper sky and low evening light, three days after the first sighting

night_bluff.label: Travancore sea bluff at night
night_bluff.anchor: The rock edge of the Travancore bluff above the sea. Nagoji sits with knees drawn up and arms resting on them, remaining seated through the palm and face close-ups. An older watchman is distant when specified. Four clusters of offshore lights replace visible masts and hulls.
night_bluff.absent: No chair, bench, stool or visible ship hull. Outside the specified cellar memory, no vaulted stone room, brazier, table or tools.
night_bluff.time: night, black water with remote points of light

character_notes.nagoji: Thick curled moustache; clean-shaven chin and jaw, smooth skin, no beard or facial scar. A tiny flush gold ear stud on the lobe with nothing hanging from it. Footwear follows the scene-specific LOOKS line, including bare feet on indoor floors and mats; ignore the boots on his sheet wherever the LOOKS line says barefoot.
character_notes.ibrahim: White turban, short grey-flecked beard and a thin pale scar from the anatomical LEFT ear to the jaw; nothing on the forehead.
character_notes.dhanaji: Stockier than Nagoji, short black beard, white Maratha pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, no sash; never a rust-red turban.
character_notes.padmini: Thick BLACK hair coiled at the nape with no grey. Cotton sari in the old Kerala drape with no stitched blouse, simple gold, long walking stick.
character_notes.revathi: Deep GREEN sari, never blue or indigo; jasmine braid; flat-coin necklace; less gold than on her sheet, with no gold armlets. The sandalwood line at the hairline is her only forehead mark: no red dot between the brows, no sindoor or red in the parting, no tali. Less gold than at her first meeting: no armlets and no anklet.
character_notes.dutch_envoys: Lead envoy: heavy, grey-streaked hair in a black ribbon queue, dark brown coat, brass buttons, lace cuffs. Second envoy: thinner, brown hair tied back, charcoal coat. Both carry black tricornes in hand or under the arm and stay bareheaded inside the hall; no wigs, no gold braid, no blue coats. In the clerk's hand insert show only the young clerk's hands, never an envoy portrait.
character_notes.karl: Cropped greying hair, bare head, sickly yellow pallor, rough cotton shirt and an awkwardly tied dhoti in place of the knee breeches, sash and buckled shoes on his sheet; no coat or uniform.
character_notes.varma: Headwear follows the scene line in his LOOKS, never the turbans drawn on his sheet: in the war hall only a narrow white cloth band over black hair pulled back, with no turban and no crest; at Tengapattanam and in the coastal audience hall the cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock-feather crest. Black hair, not the grey of the sheet's older figure. Never a crown.
